decision.assessment: The proposed release packaging addresses the confirmed signature mismatch for legacy installations with the verified AndroidDebug certificate and versionCode below 19. It can deliver the full accepted production application while retaining application data. Publishing manifest19 does not offer a downgrade to existing staging20 installations. These conclusions support the bounded approach, but do not establish successful installation or preservation of settings on a device.
decision.publication_condition: Verify the newly built artifact, both distribution endpoints and the actual old-app update path before treating the release as safe for ordinary operator rollout. Uploading an immutable candidate APK and activating the two update manifests are separate steps.
decision.confirmed_existing_defect: Legacy15 and stable19 have different signing certificates. The release-signed staging20 currently described as served by Oyster preview cannot update the verified debug-signed legacy15 in place.
decision.unresolved_acceptance_blocker: The exact legacy15 → newly built legacy-compatible19 update, including encrypted settings and PIN recovery, has not been exercised. No physical device is available, and the saved emulator log confirms failure to start because of insufficient disk space.
decision.staging_preservation_limit: Existing staging20 remains installed with its existing settings and server. This proposal neither converts it to production nor preserves a usable future release-signed update feed on the shared preview endpoint.

channel_assessment.matching_legacy_below19: Receives candidate19 from either old endpoint, subject to package, certificate, Android compatibility and old-updater verification.
channel_assessment.legacy_compatible19_after_update: Uses the old WMS preview route and sees no newer version while manifest19 remains served.
channel_assessment.release_signed_stable19: Continues using unchanged tsd-stable. No conversion or cross-signature replacement is needed.
channel_assessment.release_signed_staging20: Its updater compares manifest.versionCode > installed.versionCode. Therefore manifest19 is not offered. Source inspection confirms the updater is unchanged from stable19.
channel_assessment.uncovered_installations: Earlier APKs with another certificate, debug builds already at code19 or above, and release-signed builds below19 on an old preview URL are not proven compatible by the legacy15 certificate check.
channel_assessment.future_constraint: A static manifest cannot select an APK by installed certificate. Raising a shared preview manifest above20 with the legacy signer would expose staging20 to another signature mismatch. The present plan preserves staging20 now; it does not resolve future two-certificate distribution.
channel_assessment.rollback_constraint: Restoring an earlier manifest can stop further offers but cannot undo an installed code19 or its application changes. Do not use uninstall, data clearing or forced downgrade as rollback.

auth_profile_assessment.normal15_to19: The compared sources retain auth_store, base_url, saved_staff, the encrypted-preference algorithms and SavedStaff identity fields. Changes to AuthStore are additive recovery support rather than a replacement of the authentication store. No destructive profile migration was found in the inspected path.
auth_profile_assessment.older_unmigrated_profiles: The existing login screen invokes migrateLegacyStaffForPin. For an eligible legacy record with a saved usable server and token, successful /auth/me supplies identity fields while retaining PIN and token. Failed identity lookup leaves the raw record intact.
auth_profile_assessment.truthful_login_limit: An expired token, unavailable server or invalid identity can require password login or a later retry. Retaining stored records does not guarantee an uninterrupted authenticated session. An unmigrated record can remain stored without appearing as a PIN tile.
auth_profile_assessment.server_preservation: A saved server overrides the production default. A saved staging server therefore stays staging. The release build also rejects cleartext HTTP in relevant authentication paths; preserving an old HTTP setting does not guarantee it remains usable. Ordinary production coverage should be stated for the existing HTTPS production profiles.
auth_profile_assessment.test_limit: Existing authentication unit tests cover legacy migration, PIN retention and failed identity lookup, but use mocked storage. The crypto configuration test does not prove that an installed code15 encrypted store can be decrypted after this exact APK replacement.

release_vs_product_change.classification: Release compatibility and distribution repair using already accepted product source.
within_scope: Release build signed normally with the existing legacy-compatible certificate.
Legacy update URL override, immutable APK assets and accurate manifests.
Release-specific compatibility checks and WMS-412 evidence.
outside_scope: New authentication or automatic server-migration behavior.
Updater routing redesign or signature-verification bypass.
Staging20 conversion, later staging features or unrelated WMS fixes.
Main merge, secret inspection or key management.
release_vs_product_change.boundary: If a required check exposes an authentication or old-updater defect, this packaging assessment does not authorize silently changing product behavior. Record the concrete failure under WMS-412 and distinguish any required code correction from the proposed release-only work.

external_basis: Android updates require compatible application signing identity: [Android app signing](https://developer.android.com/studio/publish/app-signing). Using the existing debug certificate here preserves that identity; it does not make the release build debuggable.

Android uses versionCode for version ordering and downgrade protection: [Android app versioning](https://developer.android.com/studio/publish/versioning). The application's own strict greater-than check was additionally verified in source.
limitations: This is an assessment, not release acceptance or a readiness declaration.
No build, tests, installation, publication, live operator verification or production mutation was performed.
Physical-device absence and the supplied 735 MiB free-space figure come from the request; the emulator's insufficient-space failure was verified in its saved log.
Memory was used to locate relevant release history; substantive conclusions were checked against current local source, artifacts and release records.
